# A scalar-convolution criterion for compact distributions with values in an ordered space

Status: internally reconstructed theorem candidate, 2026-10-15. The argument below is mathematical work, not a claim of historical priority, independent review, formal verification, or exceptional practical capability.

## 1. Result and scope

The supplied quantum-observable candidate suggests retaining a positive real exponential tilt and perturbing only its logarithmic remainder. The extension here removes its quantitative exponential lower-bound assumption and gives an exact criterion for arbitrary compact distributions.

Let \(E\) be a real Banach space and \(C\subsetneq E\) a closed convex cone with nonempty interior. Pointedness is not needed. Write \(u\preceq_C v\) when \(v-u\in C\). Fix \(e\in\operatorname{int}C\). Let
\[
T:C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^m)\longrightarrow E
\]
be a continuous linear distribution with compact support and \(T(1)=e\). Compact support makes evaluation on every smooth function meaningful by inserting a cutoff equal to one near the support. Its real Laplace transform is
\[
\mathcal L_T(g)=T_y(e^{g\cdot y}),\qquad g\in\mathbb R^m.
\]

Define the admissible scalar class
\[
\mathscr E=\left\{p\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^m):
\int_{\mathbb R^m}e^{a|x|}|\partial^\alpha p(x)|\,dx<\infty
\ \text{for every }a\ge0,\ \alpha\right\}.
\tag{1}
\]

Call a distribution \(S\) \(C\)-positive if \(S(\phi)\in C\) for every nonnegative real \(\phi\in C_c^\infty\). **Theorem.** The following conditions are equivalent.

1. \(\mathcal L_T(g)\in\operatorname{int}C\) for every real \(g\).
2. There is a scalar probability measure \(\nu\) satisfying \(\int e^{a|z|}\nu(dz)<\infty\) for every \(a\ge0\), such that \(T*\nu\) is a \(C\)-positive distribution.
3. There is a strictly positive probability density \(p\in\mathscr E\) such that \(M=T*p\) takes values in \(C\).

Moreover, when condition 1 holds, for every \(0<\varepsilon<1\) one can choose \(p\) smooth, radial, and strictly log-concave, with
\[
(1-\varepsilon)p(x)\mathcal L_T(\nabla V(x))
\preceq_C M(x)
\preceq_C
(1+\varepsilon)p(x)\mathcal L_T(\nabla V(x)),
\qquad p=Z^{-1}e^{-V}.
\tag{2}
\]
Thus \(M(x)\in\operatorname{int}C\) at every \(x\), and
\[
\int_{\mathbb R^m}M(x)\,dx=e.
\tag{3}
\]
The output and all its derivatives are integrable in norm after multiplication by every \(e^{a|x|}\).

# A concrete dependent kernel where every smooth product kernel fails

Root construction, 15 October 2026. Independently reconstructed by the
consequence investigator. Internal analytic proof; priority unresolved.

Consider the constant-coefficient operation

    Qp = p + partial_x² partial_y² p.

Its real Laplace symbol is P(g)=1+g_x²g_y², strictly positive and already a
sum of squares. Positivity of a polynomial symbol alone does not make its
operation preserve positive densities. We construct one correlated density
for which Qp is positive, while proving that no strictly positive smooth
product density with all exponential moments can do so.

## Explicit construction and all-point bound

Set L=5, s=x²+y², t=1+s/L², ell=log t, and

    h(s)=(L/2) sqrt(t) log t,
    p(x,y)=Z^(-1) exp[-h(x²+y²)].

This is a smooth radial probability density. Its Hessian potential has
tangential eigenvalue (ell+2)/(2L sqrt(t)) and radial eigenvalue
(2t+ell)/(2L t^(3/2)), both strictly positive. Thus p is strictly
log-concave. Its potential divided by r tends to infinity, giving every
exponential moment; all finite derivatives also have those weighted integrals.

The derivatives of h are

    h1=(ell+2)/(4L sqrt(t)),
    h2=-ell/(8L³ t^(3/2)),
    h3=(3ell-2)/(16L^5 t^(5/2)),
    h4=(16-15ell)/(32L^7 t^(7/2)).

Let

    A2=h1²-h2,
    A3=-h1³+3h1h2-h3,
    A4=h1^4-6h1²h2+3h2²+4h1h3-h4.

Differentiation gives the exact identity

    (Qp)/p=1+4A2+8s A3+16x²y² A4.

Here A2 is nonnegative. In A4 its first three displayed terms are
nonnegative because h2<=0. Bound only the remaining negative terms.
The elementary inequalities, for ell>=0 and t>=1, are

    (ell+2)^3 exp(-ell/2) <= 216/e²,
    ell(ell+2)exp(-ell) <= 2,
    (3ell-2)_+ exp(-3ell/2) <= 1,
    (t-1)²/t³ <= 4/27,
    (ell+2)(2-3ell)_+ <= 4,
    (t-1)²/t^(7/2) <= 1,
    (16-15ell)_+ <= 16.

Using s=L²(t-1) and 16x²y²<=4s² yields

    (Qp)/p >= 1-B_L,
    B_L=27/(e²L)+(3/2+4/27)/L²+5/(2L³).

At L=5, B_L=0.8167364554036346...<1, so

    Qp >= 0.1832635445963654... p > 0  everywhere.

All derivatives decay sufficiently for integration by parts. Therefore
integral Qp=integral p=1: Qp is another probability density. This is an
explicit instance of the general Laplace-positive convolution criterion,
without an unspecified scale or a remotely tested numerical tail.

# Mathematical invention worker report

Date: 2026-10-15. Discovery was independent of sibling files. The supplied attachment was read fully. Parent messages provided literature leads and proof stress tests; indispensable statements were reconstructed here.

## Strongest exact result

Let \(T\) be a compactly supported Hermitian matrix distribution on \(\mathbb R^m\), normalized by \(T(1)=I_d\). The following are equivalent:

1. \(T(e^{g\cdot y})\succ0\) for every real \(g\).
2. Some scalar probability measure with every exponential moment makes its convolution with \(T\) a positive matrix distribution.
3. A smooth radial strictly log-concave scalar probability density \(p\), with every derivative integrable against every exponential weight, makes \(T*p\succ0\) at every point.

There is no quantitative lower-bound assumption on the least Laplace eigenvalue. A stronger ordered-space version holds for real Banach values in a proper closed convex cone with nonempty interior and normalized interior mass. Pointedness is unnecessary; the full-space cone is excluded.

For every \(0<\varepsilon<1\), the construction supplies
\[
(1-\varepsilon)p(x)\mathcal L_T(\nabla V(x))
\preceq (T*p)(x)
\preceq(1+\varepsilon)p(x)\mathcal L_T(\nabla V(x)).
\]

Full proof: [PROOF.md](PROOF.md).

## Mathematical operation and hard step

Retain the exact positive real exponential transform. Expand only the nonlinear remainder of the log density. The difficult part is making that remainder uniformly smaller than an arbitrarily deteriorating positivity margin.

Let \(\mu(t)\) be the minimum interior margin of \(\mathcal L_T\) on \(|g|\le t\), and absorb the distribution's order and support radius into
\[
G(t)=\max\{1,e^{R_1t}(1+t)^{N+1}/\mu(t)\}.
\]
Using a fixed smooth step, choose explicit thresholds
\[
S_n\ge2n,\qquad S_{n+1}\ge S_n+2,\qquad
S_n\ge2\log G(n+1),
\]
and set \(q(s)=1+\sum_n\theta(s-S_n)\).
Then \(q\to\infty\), every positive-order derivative is uniformly bounded, and
\(G(q(s))e^{-s}\le C e^{-s/2}\).

The radial potential
\[
V_L(x)=L\int_1^{\sqrt{1+|x/L|^2}}q(\log u)\,du
\]
is smooth and strictly convex even where \(q\) is constant. Its \(k\)-th derivative has the required bound
\(O(L^{1-k}q(\log\rho)\rho^{1-k})\). This turns the local logarithmic error into a global relative error \(O(L^{-1})\), while \(q\to\infty\) ensures every exponential moment.
